title: The Crumb Count on One Napkin
premise: After a parked snack break, we move five crumbs into rows on a paper napkin and count them twice. The answer is the same, and the next shot is the napkin.

title: The Wrapper Fold Gets One More Fold
premise: An empty snack wrapper is pressed flat and folded into increasingly small rectangles. We keep the shot through the last crease, then set it beside another small rectangle.

title: Reading the Same Portion Label Again
premise: We zoom in on one serving-size line, read it, pan away, and return to it after a cut. The package has not added any information.

title: About Eighteen Pieces, Apparently
premise: The camera lingers on a package that defines a serving as about eighteen pieces. We never open a second package to check how approximate that count is.

title: The Wrapper Color Under the Dome Light
premise: A snack wrapper is held beneath the parked car's dome light, turned once, and held there again. Its color looks a little different from each angle.

title: A Cracker Breaks at the Same Notch
premise: One cracker is pressed over a napkin until it breaks along a shallow groove. We repeat the close-up and get the same result.

title: One Bag, Three Portion Guesses
premise: Before opening a familiar bag, everyone guesses how many servings are inside from its size alone. The printed number is lower than every guess, and the bag turns out to be mostly air.

title: The Wrapper's Flavor Words, Translated
premise: The family reads the bag's flavor copy aloud, tastes a piece each, and rewrites it in plain words. 'Smoky chipotle harvest' becomes 'red, kind of.'

title: Buc-ee's Has a Serving Size for Every Pause
premise: At Buc-ee's, we walk one snack aisle and read nothing but the serving sizes off the backs of the bags. Nobody eats anything, and the aisle becomes a catalog of what each package thinks a person is.

title: The Snack Ranking Ends With the One Everyone Shares
premise: We set out to rank a few snacks by flavor, then the family has to pick one bag to split at a rest stop. The rankings collapse vote by vote until the plain pack that divides evenly wins.
